newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech 1996 FDI falls to $1.4 bln ($2.5 bln) - CNB.
newsitem.headline: Czech 1996 FDI falls to $1.4 bln ($2.5 bln) - CNB.

text.p: The Czech National Bank said on Thursday that 1996 foreign direct investment (FDI) into the Czech Republic totalled $1.4 billion, down from $2.5 billion in the previous year.
In a statement, the CNB said last year's investment put the post-Communist total for FDI at $7.1 billion from 1990-1996.
In 1996, Netherlands-based companies invested the most FDI with 18.2 percent of the total, followed by the United States (17.7 percent), and Germany (17.5 percent).
The CNB said the largest FDI last year came in a western oil consortium's purchase of a 49 percent stake in two major oil refineries.

The IOC consortium -- comprised of Italy's Agip SpA Royal Dutch/Shell and Du Pont de Nemours' unit Conoco -- paid $173 million for the stake in Ceska Rafinerska a.s., and committed to invest another $480 million over the next five years.

Second was Deutsche Telekom AG's launch of a GSM mobile telephone joint-venture with an international consortium and a Czech firm. The group won a government tender last Spring, promising to invest about $206 million in the European standard digital network.
The 1996 FDI total fell below independent expectations -- Prague's Komercni Banka a.s., had forecast $2.0 billion.
The state investment promotion agency Czechinvest said last month that FDI increased $500 million in the fourth quarter of last year, putting post-Communist FDI at about $7.2 billion.

The CNB said the largest FDI since the end of the Communist system at the end of 1989 came from Germany with 27.5 percent of the total, followed by the Netherlands (14.5 percent), and the United States (14.4 percent).
The 1995 figures, the largest for any single year, were helped significantly by a $1.32 billion equity expansion giving a Dutch-Swiss PTT consortium a 27 percent stake in SPT Telecom a.s..
